generate.title: Create curriculum entries
generate.body: Creates the curriculum entries the academic year's classes are missing according to {plan}: one entry per class and subject the plan gives time in the class's year group. Existing entries are never changed, teaching groups are not created and no teacher is set — do that afterwards under Curriculum entries. Modern languages are never put on a class, and of Swedish and Swedish as a second language a class gets only one.
generate.noYears: The school has no academic year yet.
generate.lengthHintCommon: The suggestion {minutes} is the length the year's entries use most.
generate.lengthHintDefault: The year has no entries yet, so the suggestion is {minutes} minutes.
generate.splitLabel: Split the remainder so the target is met without surplus
generate.splitHint: The target is met without surplus where possible: 175 minutes at 60 becomes 2 × 60 + 1 × 55, and 120 at 80 becomes 1 × 80 + 1 × 40. Beside two or more lessons, a remainder of at most half the length is added to one of them instead, so 200 at 60 becomes 1 × 80 + 2 × 60.
generate.roundUpHint: Whole lessons, rounded up: 175 minutes at 60 becomes 3 × 60, 5 above target.
generate.splitNote: {count, plural, one {# entry gets} other {# entries get}} lengths other than whole lessons of the chosen length, so the target is met without surplus. Make uniform gives whole lessons instead.
generate.surplusHintSplit: The remainder becomes a lesson of its own or is added to another, so the entry meets the target; a small difference can remain where the timetable's 5-minute steps or 15-minute minimum length require it.

constraints.title: Availability
constraints.subtitle: When teachers, rooms or classes are unavailable
constraints.empty: No constraints. The AI engine will treat every resource as always available.
constraints.preferencesHint: State what should preferably happen, as opposed to the absolute rules above. The engine tries to honour these but will break a wish rather than make the week unschedulable.
constraints.preferenceWeightHint: How much the engine may give up elsewhere to honour the wish. The scale is the one the optimization profile uses: 5 weighs the same as the other preferences, above 10 the wish starts overriding goals such as spreading subjects across the week.
constraints.gradeHint: The rule applies to every class and teaching group with students in the range.
constraints.locksHint: A lock is absolute: the subject's lessons may only be in the rooms you choose. If it cannot be honoured the timetable is refused, naming the rule that is impossible — unlike the wishes below, which the solver weighs against everything else.
constraints.locksEmpty: No locks. Every room is allowed for every subject.
constraints.ruleGradesHint: The rule applies to a group whose years all fit inside the span. A group spanning 6-7 is therefore not reached by a rule for 7-9.

frameTimes.title: Frame times
frameTimes.subtitle: The hours each stage may be timetabled within
frameTimes.empty: No frame times. The whole school day is open to every year.
frameTimes.hint: A frame time says when a stage MAY have lessons. Everything outside it is closed — the engine places nothing there, the timetable warns if you drag something into it, and the gap search stops offering the time.
frameTimes.overlapHint: Frame times reaching the same group all apply at once, so the narrowest window wins. Writing “08:00–15:00 every day” and “08:00–13:00 Friday” makes Friday 08:00–13:00 with nothing to remove.
frameTimes.effectiveHint: Computed from the rows above, one stage per row.
frameTimes.duplicate: A frame time already exists for those years on that day.
frameTimes.changeoverHint: Time a class or teacher needs to move. The solver leaves at least this much between two consecutive lessons. 0 means no margin. Several matching frames give the largest — a frame is a bound, a margin is a floor.
frameTimes.offerWholeSchool: Add a frame for the whole school

lunchServings.title: Lunch sittings
lunchServings.subtitle: When each stage eats, and in what order
lunchServings.seatsHint: Left blank, the dining hall's own seat count from the lunch card applies.
lunchServings.empty: No sittings. The whole lunch window is open to every year at once.
lunchServings.hint: You write when a stage eats. The solver decides which class goes when inside the window, and splits a stage bigger than the hall into several waves.
lunchServings.overlapHint: Sittings reaching the same group add up — a year 6-7 group may eat at both the 4-6 and the 7-9 sitting. A row for one weekday replaces the every-day row that day rather than widening it.
lunchServings.noLunch: Lunch is not defined — sittings mean nothing until it is.
lunchServings.flowSubtitle: Who eats when, day by day — the list the kitchen can print

lunchServings.windowsHint: Computed from the rows above, with the rule the solver uses.

breaks.title: Holidays and staff days
breaks.intro: The days the academic year has but the timetable does not. They are deducted from the curriculum's hours, and saving one removes any published lessons inside it from the calendar.
breaks.namePlaceholder: Autumn half term, Staff day, Work experience year 9…
breaks.datesHint: Both days are included. A single staff day has the same date in both fields.
breaks.gradeHint: The break applies to every class with students in the span. Teaching groups without a year of their own are not affected — their lessons stay and remain visible in the calendar.
breaks.deletesWarning: Saving removes published lessons inside the period from the calendar. Lessons that have already happened, been cancelled, or had attendance recorded are left alone. Shortening or deleting the break does not bring back lessons that were already removed.
breaks.removedLessons: {name} saved. {count, plural, =1 {1 published lesson was removed from the calendar.} other {# published lessons were removed from the calendar.}}
breaks.removedNone: {name} saved. No published lessons needed removing.
breaks.deleteBody: The break leaves the list and the curriculum's hours count that week as taught again. The lessons removed when the break was entered do not come back.
breaks.empty: No holidays entered for this academic year. The curriculum's hours then count every calendar week as taught, which runs roughly 8–10 weeks high across a Swedish academic year.
breaks.noYear: Create and activate an academic year first.
breaks.loadFailed: The list of holidays could not be fetched.
breaks.loadFailedHint: No list is shown, because an empty one would mean the school has no holidays at all. Switch the year above to try again.
breaks.tableCaption: The academic year's holidays and staff days, earliest first. Each row is a period the school is not teaching, and the curriculum's hours deduct it.

credits.subject: Subject
credits.subjectNone: No subject — counts as teaching time
credits.countsAsNotCounted: {minutes} min {subject}, {scope} — the subject does not count toward the timplan, so the time does not count

staffing.title: Reports
staffing.subtitle: Staffing: planned, scheduled and delivered per teacher
staffing.loadFailed: The reconciliation could not be read.
staffing.rangeCrossed: From is after To. The figures below are for the last valid period.
staffing.empty: No teacher has planned, scheduled or delivered time in the period.
staffing.comparison: Planned and scheduled are compared {from} – {to}. Model: {model}. Minutes, rounded per row.
staffing.tableCaption: Planned, scheduled and delivered per teacher in minutes, with substitute time and losses. Each row expands per subject and group.
staffing.footGroupLosses: Every lost lesson counts once, in the pupils' lesson minutes and not per teacher.
staffing.footDefinition: Delivered is lessons that were held, are not cancelled and have at least one teacher — the same definition of held time as Timplan › Coverage, but with every subject, including those that do not count toward the timplan: a teacher's mentor time is teaching too.
staffing.footCredit: A held lesson is credited to the teacher rows on it: the lead and the co-teacher at the row's percentage, a substitute at 100 %. A lead or co-teacher left beside a substitute is credited to nobody.
staffing.footCoTeacher: Covered by others reads the master schedule's current teacher and co-teacher, not whoever was scheduled that day. A substitute replaces every teacher row on the lesson, so a co-teacher who was there counts here and not as delivered.
staffing.footScheduled: Scheduled is today's master schedule counted over the period; changes during the period show in Delivered. Parked lessons do not count as scheduled but count as delivered if they were held.
staffing.footGrade: Planned is counted per school day in the period, holidays by the group's own grade, as publishing does. The weekly report under Staffing counts a standard week.
staffing.footAhead: Upcoming: lessons in the period that have not ended yet. Cancelled upcoming lessons count as neither lost nor upcoming. Holidays and staff days are not a loss.
staffing.footRounding: Each row, each teacher's total and the totals are rounded on their own (rounded per row): a teacher's total is not always the sum of the rows under it.
staffing.footFactor: Model Factor: the minutes are counted time, lesson time × the subject's factor. The factor is the school's per subject and applies to every school year; changing it changes earlier years' figures too.

notice.STAFFING_NOTHING_PUBLISHED: No schedule is published to the calendar for the school year. Delivered is empty, and planned and scheduled are not compared.
notice.STAFFING_RANGE_CLAMPED: The period was shortened to the school year: {from} – {to}.
notice.STAFFING_RANGE_INCLUDES_FUTURE: The period reaches today ({asOfDate}) or later: lessons that have not ended show as Upcoming, while planned counts the whole day.
notice.STAFFING_RANGE_BEFORE_PUBLISHED: The calendar starts {publishedFrom}: planned and scheduled are compared from that day, so the time before does not look like a deficit.
notice.STAFFING_RANGE_AFTER_PUBLISHED: The calendar is published until {publishedThrough}: planned and scheduled are compared until that day.
notice.STAFFING_RANGE_HAS_GAPS: The calendar has gaps between publishes, {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} between {from} and {through}. The figures are not adjusted for them.
notice.STAFFING_RANGE_PARTIAL_WEEKS: The comparison {from} – {to} starts or ends mid-week. Planned counts a fifth of the week per school day, scheduled and delivered count each lesson on its own day, so they can differ even when everything went to plan. Choose whole weeks, Monday to Friday, to compare line by line.
notice.STAFFING_LEAD_BESIDE_SUBSTITUTE: {lessons, plural, one {# held lesson has a teacher left beside a substitute. The time is credited to the substitute and not to the teacher.} other {# held lessons have a teacher left beside a substitute. The time is credited to the substitute and not to them.}}

notice.ADMIN: {name}: is an administrator in SchemaPro and is reported as a teacher. Check OmfRektor and OmfLedn.

notice.NO_SPAN: {name}: {line} has no grade, so the row has no type of activity.
notice.GRADE_OUT_OF_SCOPE: Grade {grade} is outside the file (preschool class to grade 9); the row has no type of activity.

notice.GRADE_WITHOUT_TIMPLAN: Grade {grade} has no timplan for the school year and is reported as compulsory school.
notice.ALL_LEFT_OUT: {name}: the teaching on one row has no SCB column. State the subjects by hand.

gaps.title: Gaps and idle time
gaps.intro: Three questions asked of the base schedule: when are these free at the same time, where are the idle gaps, and who is free right then. All of it is computed in the browser from the schedule you already have — nothing is saved.
gaps.emptyHint: Generate or lay a schedule first, and there will be gaps to search.
gaps.freeHint: Pick the classes, teachers and rooms that must be free at the same time. The answer is the whole window, not every fifteen minutes — so you can see how much room you actually have to move into.
gaps.freeNobody: Pick at least one class, teacher or room — otherwise the question is about nobody.
gaps.freeNone: No shared free time of at least {minutes} for {who}. Try a shorter length or fewer of them.
gaps.freeCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 free window} other {# free windows}} for {who}
gaps.idleHint: An idle gap is a hole between the first and the last lesson of a day — time somebody spends waiting at school. It is counted per pupil, so a gap can be half a class while the other half is in a lesson. Time before the first and after the last lesson does not count; they are not here for it. Heaviest week first.
gaps.idleLunchWindow: {minutes} min of lunch is credited once a day, to the first gap in the window that can hold it.
gaps.idleLunchOff: No lunch break is configured, so no gap is credited for a meal.
gaps.idlePupilTime: The timetable plan gives some lessons extra time for the pupils — changing before and showering after. That time counts as occupied, so a gap that looks empty on the grid may be missing here: the class is in the changing room, and the timetable editor will not let a lesson in there either.
gaps.idleNone: No idle gaps of at least {minutes} anywhere in the schedule.
gaps.idleCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 class or teacher has idle gaps} other {# classes and teachers have idle gaps}}
gaps.idleSummary: Up to {total} idle in a single week, longest gap {worst}
gaps.idleStudents: {free} of {total, plural, =1 {1 pupil free} other {# pupils free}}
gaps.lengthLegend: Gaps are labelled by the waiting time left once lunch is subtracted — the same time the totals are counted in: under 40 minutes is short, 40–79 medium, 80 minutes and up long. A 1 h 40 min gap with 30 min of lunch therefore counts as 70 minutes: medium.
gaps.whoHint: Give a day and a time — the question you ask when you need a substitute on Wednesday at ten. Every class, teacher and room is tested on its own.
gaps.whoInvalid: The end time must be after the start time.
gaps.whoCount: {groups, plural, =1 {1 class} other {# classes}}, {teachers, plural, =1 {1 teacher} other {# teachers}} and {rooms, plural, =1 {1 room} other {# rooms}} are free {day} {start}–{end}

rasts.hint: A break is minutes of the day a stage is free. The solver places no lessons across them, and they appear in the pupil's, guardian's and teacher's schedule. Several breaks a day is normal — every matching row applies.
rasts.name: Name
rasts.lessonBefore: Require a lesson before the break
rasts.lessonBeforeHint: The class must have at least one lesson between the previous break or lunch — or the start of the day — and this break, if it is still at school afterwards. Without it, a day may open with a break.
rasts.empty: No breaks have been entered. Without them the solver places lessons back to back.
rasts.weekHint: The rows above read as a week. A day-specific break replaces only the every-day break whose time it overlaps — the others still stand that day.
rasts.deleteBody: {name} will be removed. The solver may then place lessons in that time on its next run.

teacherWorkTime.hardRuleHint: These are hard requirements: the solver refuses the whole week if it cannot fit them, and names the teacher's row that did not work out.
teacherWorkTime.lunchMinutesHint: Unbroken minutes of lunch the teacher is owed. Leave empty if no lunch rule applies.
teacherWorkTime.windowHint: Lunch must both start and end inside the window. The length and the two times belong together — either all three, or none of them.
teacherWorkTime.restMinutesHint: At least this long between the last lesson of one day and the first of the next.
teacherWorkTime.emptyMeansNoRule: All four fields empty means no working-time rule applies to this teacher. A suggestion is not stored until you press Save.
teacherWorkTime.useSuggestion: Use the suggestion: 30 min between 10:30 and 13:30, and 11 hours of rest
teacherWorkTime.cleared: The working-time rule has been removed.
teacherWorkTime.noRule: No working-time rule. The solver promises this teacher neither lunch nor rest.
teacherWorkTime.summaryRestHours: At least {hours} hours of rest between two days
teacherWorkTime.summaryRestHoursMinutes: At least {hours} h {minutes} min of rest between two days
teacherWorkTime.lunchTrioIncomplete: The length of lunch and its window belong together. Fill in all three fields, or empty all three.
teacherWorkTime.lunchMinutesOutOfRange: Lunch is given in whole minutes, between {min} and {max}.
teacherWorkTime.lunchMinutesOffGrid: Lunch must be a whole multiple of {step} minutes — the solver's grid is {step} minutes.
teacherWorkTime.lunchWindowBackwards: The end of the window must fall after its start.
teacherWorkTime.lunchWindowTooNarrow: The window is {window} minutes wide and does not hold a lunch of {minutes} minutes.
teacherWorkTime.lunchWindowOffGrid: The window's times must fall on whole {step}-minute intervals, for example 10:30 or 10:35.
teacherWorkTime.restOutOfRange: Daily rest is given in whole minutes, between {min} and {max}.

staffing.title: Staffing
staffing.subtitle: Who teaches how many minutes a week, in which subjects and against which target
staffing.noYear: Create and activate an academic year first.
staffing.empty: No teachers with a post or a curriculum entry for this year. Enter posts on the teachers' rows under People, or assign teachers on the curriculum entries.
staffing.loadFailed: The report could not be fetched
staffing.loadFailedHint: No figures are shown, because they would read zero for the wrong reason. Switch the year in the picker above to try again.
staffing.noTargetBody: The school has not chosen a full-time teaching target, so no teacher can be compared against a goal and every row reads No target. The agreement states no weekly measure — the target is the school's own decision.
staffing.kpiUnqualifiedNotRecordedHint: The list is empty because the school has recorded no qualifications at all — not because everyone is qualified.
staffing.weekHintStandard: The standard week weighs a whole-year entry 1, alternate weeks 0.5 and a dated entry by its share of the year's teaching weeks, holidays deducted. The subject columns always show the standard week.
staffing.weekHintPeak: The peak week is the single heaviest ISO week — where a term course and a year course collide although neither is heavy alone. The Teaching column shows it; the subject columns show the standard week.
staffing.unitHintPercent: Percent of employment is the employment percentage × the subject's share of the teacher's teaching — Statistics Sweden's share of post per subject. Empty for a teacher without a post.
staffing.tableCaption: Staffing per teacher and subject. Cells are minutes per standard week or percent of employment; the last columns are employment, target, teaching, duties, balance and share of target. Teachers over target come first.
staffing.drawerUnqualified: {count, plural, one {# assignment without qualification} other {# assignments without qualification}}
staffing.employmentHint: The post applies to {year}. The whole row is rewritten when you save.
staffing.signatureHint: At most eight characters, unique per year.
staffing.targetOverrideHint: Leave empty to derive the target from the school's full-time figure × (post − reduction), rounded to five minutes. 0 means the post holds no teaching.
staffing.derivedNoTarget: Target: no full-time figure set for the school
staffing.derivedRegulated: Regulated working time: {hours} h/year over {days} working days
staffing.noEmployment: No post recorded for this year. The teacher counts without a target until one is saved.
staffing.qualificationsHint: The whole list is saved at once: what you see is what applies. One subject per row — maths 1–6 and 7–9 is written as 1–9.
staffing.noQualifications: No qualifications recorded. Substitute suggestions and the qualification check fall back to who has a curriculum entry in the subject.
staffing.unstaffedHint: Curriculum entries without a teacher. Suggest teachers ranks the school's teachers by qualification, whether they already teach the group and how much room they have left — one click assigns.
staffing.unstaffedEmpty: Every curriculum entry has a teacher.
staffing.policyHint: One row for the school. The target decides what each teacher is compared with; the checks decide what happens when a teacher is put on a curriculum entry.
staffing.riktmarkeSource: 1 080 min/wk (630 h/year) is Vimmerby municipality's full-time target in its staffing principles; the Sveriges Lärare survey shows a full-time median of 1 090 min/wk (P10 850, P90 1 280). The agreement (Bilaga M) states no weekly teaching measure, so the figure is the school's own decision.
staffing.toleranceHint: How many percent over target a teacher may be before the row reads Over target.
staffing.modelHint: Minutes: a teacher's load is their lesson minutes. Factor: load = lesson time × the subject's factor (the school's setting per subject). The pupils' lesson minutes are not affected.
staffing.refuseHint: Refuse means an assignment that breaks the check is not saved, with a sentence saying why. Warn saves and shows the sentence. A substitute is always warned, never refused.
staffing.candidateOverAfter: {minutes} min/wk over target with this row
staffing.candidateHint: Qualification and remaining minutes per teacher, from the staffing. The school's settings decide whether an assignment is warned about or refused when it is saved.
staffing.problem_percentRequired: Enter the employment percentage. A post without a percentage is no post.
staffing.problem_percentOutOfRange: The employment percentage is above 0 and at most 100, with at most {decimals} decimals.
staffing.problem_reductionOutOfRange: The reduction is a percentage between 0 and 100, with at most {decimals} decimals.
staffing.problem_reductionAbovePercent: The reduction ({reduction} %) cannot exceed the post ({percent} %).
staffing.problem_targetOutOfRange: The own target is whole minutes per week, at most {max}.
staffing.problem_signatureTooLong: The signature is at most {max} characters.
staffing.problem_noteTooLong: The note is at most {max} characters.
staffing.problem_spanReversed: Row {row}: the highest grade ({max}) cannot be below the lowest ({min}). A span is written 7–9, not 9–7.
staffing.problem_validityReversed: Row {row}: the end date is before the start date.
staffing.problem_duplicateSubject: Row {row} has the same subject as row {first}. One qualification per subject — write the span as one.
staffing.problem_riktmarkeOutOfRange: The target is whole minutes per week, between 1 and {max}. Leave it empty for no comparison.
staffing.problem_regulatedOutOfRange: Regulated working time is whole hours per year, between 1 and {max}.
staffing.problem_annualOutOfRange: Annual working time is whole hours per year, between 1 and {max}.
staffing.problem_regulatedAboveAnnual: Regulated working time ({regulated} h) does not fit in the annual working time ({annual} h).
staffing.problem_workDaysOutOfRange: Working days are whole days, between 1 and {max}.
staffing.problem_semesterHoursOutOfRange: The annual-leave contract's weekly hours are above 0 and at most {max}, with at most one decimal.
staffing.problem_toleranceOutOfRange: The tolerance is whole percent between 0 and {max}.
staffing.barCountedDuty: of which {minutes} min duties counted as teaching
staffing.barDuty: {minutes} min other duties, outside the target
staffing.dutyCellCounted: of which {minutes} min count as teaching
staffing.kpiBottlenecksNotComputedHint: Without a single recorded qualification there is no knowing how much room the qualified teachers have left — so no figure, not zero.
staffing.suggestFailed: The suggestions could not be loaded. Close and open again.
staffing.suggestCharge: The row charges its teacher {minutes} min/wk.
staffing.suggestNoQualifications: The school has recorded no qualifications, so the list is ranked by who already teaches the subject or had the group in it last year.
staffing.suggestEmpty: The school has no active teachers to suggest.
staffing.suggestWouldExceed: Over the limit with this row
staffing.suggestUnassign: Remove the teacher from the row
staffing.bottlenecksHint: Per subject: the minutes the unstaffed rows would charge a teacher, against what the teachers qualified in the subject have left to their targets. Short means the rows cannot be staffed without someone going over target.
staffing.bottlenecksNotComputed: No qualifications recorded, so the qualified teachers' capacity cannot be computed. Record qualifications on the teachers' rows and the bottlenecks appear here.
staffing.bottlenecksEmpty: No unstaffed rows, so no demand to compare.
staffing.bottlenecksCaption: Subject bottlenecks: demand from unstaffed rows against the qualified teachers' remaining minutes, shortages first.
staffing.bottleneckRows: {count, plural, one {# unstaffed row} other {# unstaffed rows}}
staffing.dutiesHint: Other duties in {year}: mentoring, subject lead, staff meetings, break duty. A duty with a fixed time can block that time in the timetable.
staffing.dutiesLoadFailed: The duties could not be loaded.
staffing.noDuties: No duties recorded for the year.
staffing.removeDutyBody: The duty and its minutes leave the teacher's post.
staffing.removeDutyBodySlot: The duty and its minutes leave the teacher's post, and the time it blocked in the timetable is free again.
staffing.dutyBlockTimeHint: The teacher becomes unavailable at that time every week, so scheduling leaves it free. The time is removed with the duty.
staffing.dutiesTotal: {count, plural, one {# duty} other {# duties}}, {minutes} min/wk in all

engineMessages.AVAIL_CONSTRAINT_BLOCKS_LESSONS: A constraint on {kind, select, TEACHER {a teacher} ROOM {room {resource}} STUDENT_GROUP {class {resource}} other {years {grades}}} {day, select, 0 {on {date}} 1 {on Mondays} 2 {on Tuesdays} 3 {on Wednesdays} 4 {on Thursdays} 5 {on Fridays} 6 {on Saturdays} 7 {on Sundays} other {on day {day}}} {start}-{end} blocks lessons that have to be placed.
engineMessages.CONFLICT_CORE_SUMMARY: No timetable satisfies every rule. Start with the causes listed below: together they are enough to make the week impossible, but the solver reports a sufficient set rather than the smallest one, so some of them may carry no blame.
engineMessages.CONFLICT_NO_CORE: No timetable satisfies every rule, and the solver could not name which of them collide.
engineMessages.CONFLICT_NO_CORE_GUESS: Total teaching demand likely exceeds available room or teacher time. Review lessons per week, unavailable windows, and room capacity.
engineMessages.DEMAND_CLIQUE_HOURS_SHORT: Too many lessons for the hours: student group {group} and the {sharingGroups, plural, one {# teaching group} other {# teaching groups}} sharing its pupils may never overlap, and between them need {demandMinutes} minutes of lessons a week, but the frame times, the locked lessons and the lunch leave at most {capacityMinutes}. Widen the frame, unlock a lesson in the middle of the day, or move the lunch window.
engineMessages.DEMAND_REQUIREMENTS_EXCEED_WEEK: Lessons of {requirements, plural, one {# requirement} other {# requirements}} need {demandMinutes} minutes a week and the week offers {capacityMinutes}.
engineMessages.FRAME_NO_WINDOW_FOR_REQUIREMENT: The frame times leave no room for requirement {requirement} ({grades, select, any {years unknown} other {years {grades}}}): its {minutes}-minute lessons need a window, and the widest any day still offers is {remaining} minutes.
engineMessages.MARGIN_NO_WINDOW_FOR_REQUIREMENT: The time around the lessons of requirement {requirement} ({grades, select, any {years unknown} other {years {grades}}}) leaves them no day to run on: its {minutes}-minute lessons take {before} minutes before and {after} minutes after for the pupils, {changeover, select, 0 {with no changeover between lessons} other {plus {changeover} minutes of changeover between lessons}}, and the widest any day then leaves for the lesson itself is {remaining} minutes. Shorten the lessons, shorten those margins, or widen the window they all have to fit inside.
engineMessages.INPUT_CONSTRAINT_TIME_OFF_GRID: The constraint on {kind, select, TEACHER {a teacher} ROOM {room {resource}} STUDENT_GROUP {class {resource}} other {years {grades}}} runs {start}-{end}, which does not fit the {slotMinutes}-minute scheduling grid or falls outside the school day.
engineMessages.INPUT_LESSON_LENGTH_OFF_GRID: Requirement {requirement} asks for {minutes}-minute lessons, which do not fit the {slotMinutes}-minute scheduling grid. Use a whole multiple of {slotMinutes} minutes.
engineMessages.INPUT_LESSON_LONGER_THAN_DAY: Requirement {requirement} asks for {minutes}-minute lessons, which are longer than the school day.
engineMessages.INPUT_MODEL_TOO_LARGE: This week is too large to build: about {variables} model variables against a limit of {limit}. The usual causes are rooms with many different capacities, constraints that each touch many lessons, and very high per-teacher lesson loads.
engineMessages.ROOM_MODEL_TOO_LARGE: There are too many rooms to re-deal in one go: about {variables} model variables against a limit of {limit}. The model grows with how many lessons may move and how many rooms each may use. Lock the lessons whose room is settled (a locked lesson keeps both its time and its room), or give subjects room rules that narrow where they may go, and try again.
engineMessages.INPUT_NO_REQUIREMENTS: The timplan is empty: there is nothing to place. Add at least one row.
engineMessages.INPUT_NO_ROOMS: No rooms are registered, so no lesson can be given one.
engineMessages.INPUT_TOO_MANY_LESSONS: The week holds {lessons} lessons, more than the {limit} this engine will place in one run. Split the run, or reduce lessons per week.
engineMessages.LUNCH_AVAILABILITY_LEAVES_NO_BREAK: An availability constraint leaves student group {group} no {minutes}-minute lunch break inside {windowStart}-{windowEnd} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}}. Shorten the constraint, widen the lunch window, or shorten the break.
engineMessages.LUNCH_BREAK_IS_THE_DIFFERENCE: The {lunchMinutes}-minute lunch break is what leaves no room: without it the week would hold these lessons ({freeMinutes} minutes free).
engineMessages.LUNCH_CAUSES_LEAVE_NO_BREAK: Together, {causes, select, locked {locked lessons} closed {availability constraints} declared {the declared lunch sittings} locked_closed {locked lessons and availability constraints} locked_declared {locked lessons and the declared lunch sittings} closed_declared {availability constraints and the declared lunch sittings} locked_closed_declared {locked lessons, availability constraints and the declared lunch sittings} other {these rules}} leave student group {group} no {minutes}-minute lunch break inside {windowStart}-{windowEnd} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}}.
engineMessages.LUNCH_CLASSES_EAT_DAILY: The classes named here take a lunch break every school day.
engineMessages.LUNCH_CLASSES_FILL_THE_HALL_DAILY: The classes named here bring their students to the hall every school day.
engineMessages.LUNCH_GROUP_LARGER_THAN_HALL: Student group {group} brings {students, plural, one {# student} other {# students}} to lunch, more than the dining hall's {seats} seats.
engineMessages.LUNCH_HALL_CANNOT_FEED_THE_SCHOOL: The dining hall cannot feed the school on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}}: {students, plural, one {# student} other {# students}} eating {minutes} minutes each need {needed} student-minutes, and {seats} seats over {windowStart}-{windowEnd} offer {offered}. Add seats, widen the lunch window, or shorten the meal.
engineMessages.LUNCH_HALL_CANNOT_SEAT_CLASSES: The dining hall's {seats} seats cannot seat the {classes, plural, one {# class} other {# classes}} named ({students, plural, one {# student} other {# students}}) at the lunch starts their days leave them, in {lunchMinutes}-minute sittings between {windowStart} and {windowEnd}. Add seats, widen the lunch window or the sittings, or free the starts a frame, a lock or a constraint takes away.
engineMessages.LUNCH_LESSONS_FILL_THE_DAY: The lessons of the classes named here fill the day so completely around the break that few lunch starts are left for it.
engineMessages.LUNCH_LESSONS_FILL_THE_FRAMED_DAY: The lessons of the classes named here fill their frame time {window} so completely around the break that few lunch starts are left for it.
engineMessages.LUNCH_STARTS_PLACED_BY_HAND: The classes named here have a lunch the school placed by hand, and the other lunches have to fit around it.
engineMessages.LUNCH_PLACEMENT_OFF_GRID: The lunch placed by hand for student group {group} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}} starts at {start}, which does not fit the {slotMinutes}-minute scheduling grid or the school day. Move it to a time the day holds.
engineMessages.LUNCH_PLACEMENT_COLLIDES: The lunch placed by hand for student group {group} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}} at {start} lands on {what, select, locked {a locked lesson} closed {time reserved for the class} day {a day the class is not at school} other {time the class cannot give up}}. Move the lunch, or change what it lands on.
engineMessages.LUNCH_PLACED_BY_HAND: The lunch placed by hand for student group {group} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}} at {start} is one of the rules that cannot all hold at once. Move it, or remove it and let the solver place the meal.
engineMessages.LUNCH_LOCKED_LESSONS_LEAVE_NO_BREAK: Locked lessons leave student group {group} no {minutes}-minute lunch break inside {windowStart}-{windowEnd} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}}.
engineMessages.LUNCH_NO_PLACEMENT_FOR_CLASSES: No placement of the lunch breaks works for the {classes, plural, one {# class} other {# classes}} named: their lessons, sittings, frame times, locked lessons and constraints leave no day that holds both the lessons and the break. Widen the frame or the lunch window, or unlock a lesson in the middle of the day.
engineMessages.LUNCH_NO_PLACEMENT_SEATS_UNDECIDED: No placement of the lunch breaks satisfies the lunch window, the sittings, the frame times, the locked lessons and the dining hall's {seats} seats together for the {classes, plural, one {# class} other {# classes}} named. The solver ran out of time before it could say whether the seats are the difference.
engineMessages.LUNCH_NO_SERVING_FOR_GROUP: No lunch sitting leaves student group {group} room for a {minutes}-minute meal on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}}. Widen the sitting, shorten the break, or check the stage's frame times.
engineMessages.LUNCH_SEATS_CANNOT_STAGGER: Lunch cannot be staggered within the dining hall's {seats} seats.
engineMessages.LUNCH_SEATS_CAP: The dining hall's {seats} seats are all it holds at one time.
engineMessages.LUNCH_SERVING_CANNOT_FEED_STAGE: The {servingStart}-{servingEnd} sitting for years {grades} cannot feed {students, plural, one {# student} other {# students}} {minutes} minutes each with {seats} seats. Widen the sitting, add seats, or split the stage across two sittings.
engineMessages.LUNCH_STARTS_NARROWED_BY_SITTING_OR_FRAM: A lunch sitting or a frame time narrows when the classes named here may eat.
engineMessages.LUNCH_STARTS_TAKEN_BY_LOCKED_LESSONS: Locked lessons take lunch starts away from the classes named here.
engineMessages.LUNCH_STARTS_TAKEN_BY_RESERVATION: An availability constraint takes lunch starts away from the classes named here.
engineMessages.LUNCH_WINDOW_OFF_GRID: The lunch window {windowStart}-{windowEnd} and its {minutes}-minute break do not fit the {slotMinutes}-minute scheduling grid. Use whole multiples of {slotMinutes} minutes.
engineMessages.LUNCH_WINDOW_SHORTER_THAN_BREAK: The lunch window {windowStart}-{windowEnd} is shorter than the {minutes}-minute lunch break it has to hold.
engineMessages.PROBE_NOTHING_HELPED: No timetable was found within {budget} s, and none of the {rules, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}} probed made one appear inside {slice} s each. The week may simply be large; try a longer budget.
engineMessages.PROBE_ONE_RULE_HELPED: No timetable was found within {budget} s, but relaxing a single rule made the same week solve. {rules, plural, one {The rule is listed below} other {The # rules are listed below}} — a measurement, not a proof.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_CHANGEOVER: With the margin between lessons set to 0, a timetable was found in {seconds} s.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_PUPIL_BUFFERS: With the extra time the pupils need before and after their lessons set to 0, a timetable was found in {seconds} s.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_TEACHER_LUNCH: With the teachers' own guaranteed lunch switched off, a timetable was found in {seconds} s.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_TEACHER_REST: With the teachers' own minimum rest between two teaching days switched off, a timetable was found in {seconds} s.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_DINING_SEATS: With the dining hall's seat limit removed, a timetable was found in {seconds} s.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_LUNCH: With the guaranteed lunch break switched off, a timetable was found in {seconds} s.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_LESSON_BEFORE_RAST: With the requirement of a lesson before a break dropped, a timetable was found in {seconds} s. The breaks themselves were left in place.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_RASTS: With the rasts removed, a timetable was found in {seconds} s.
engineMessages.PROBE_SOLVED_WITHOUT_SERVINGS: With the lunch sittings per stage removed, so that the whole window was open to every stage, a timetable was found in {seconds} s.
engineMessages.RAST_NO_LESSON_FITS_BEFORE_IT: The classes named here require a lesson before a break, and their week leaves nowhere to put one: between the start of their day — or their previous break or lunch — and that break, no lesson of theirs fits. Move the break, shorten a lesson, or turn the requirement off for that break.
engineMessages.RAST_DEMANDS_A_LESSON_THAT_CANNOT_FIT: The break at {rast} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}} asks for a lesson before it, and none can fit: {grades, select, any {classes with unknown years} other {years {grades}}} have {remaining, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} between {opens} — {bound, select, lunch {the earliest their lunch can end} closed {what a reservation leaves of it} other {where the stretch opens}} — and that break, and their shortest lesson is {minutes} minutes. They can therefore never be at school after that break, and the days that are left hold {capacityMinutes} minutes against the {demandMinutes} their lessons need. Move the break, shorten the meal or widen its window, free the minutes a reservation holds, or turn the requirement off for that break.
engineMessages.RAST_NO_STRETCH_FOR_REQUIREMENT: The rasts leave no room for requirement {requirement} ({grades, select, any {years unknown} other {years {grades}}}): its {minutes}-minute lessons need an unbroken stretch, and the longest any day still offers is {remaining} minutes. Shorten a rast, widen the frame time, or split the lesson.
engineMessages.ROOM_LOCK_LEAVES_NO_ROOM: A room lock leaves requirement {requirement} ({grades, select, any {years unknown} other {years {grades}}}) nowhere to go: the rooms it names are too small, of the wrong type, or reserved for other years. Widen the lock, name another room, or change the room.
engineMessages.ROOM_LOCK_WEEK_TOO_SMALL: Room locks put {requirements, plural, one {# requirement} other {# requirements}} into {rooms, plural, one {# room} other {# rooms}} that cannot hold them: they need {neededMinutes} minutes a week and those rooms offer {offeredMinutes}. Name another room, or narrow which years the lock applies to.
engineMessages.ROOM_NONE_ELIGIBLE_FOR_REQUIREMENT: No room fits requirement {requirement} ({grades, select, any {years unknown} other {years {grades}}}): it needs room for {groupSize, plural, one {# student} other {# students}} and a room of type {roomType, select, any {any type} other {{roomType}}}.
engineMessages.ROOM_NO_ROOM_FOR_REQUIREMENT: Requirement {requirement} needs a room that holds {groupSize, plural, one {# student} other {# students}}.
engineMessages.ROOM_NO_ROOM_OF_TYPE_FOR_REQUIREMENT: Requirement {requirement} needs a room of type {roomType} that holds {groupSize, plural, one {# student} other {# students}}.
engineMessages.STAFF_TEACHER_NOT_QUALIFIED: {role, select, CO_TEACHER {The co-teacher} SUBSTITUTE {The substitute} other {The teacher}} has no qualification in {subject}{grades, select, any {} other { for years {grades}}}.
engineMessages.STAFF_TEACHER_OVER_TARGET: {role, select, CO_TEACHER {The co-teacher} SUBSTITUTE {The substitute} other {The teacher}} would carry {minutes} minutes a week against a target of {target} (the limit is {limit} with the {tolerance} % tolerance).
engineMessages.STAFF_UNSTAFFED_REQUIREMENTS: {count, plural, one {# curriculum entry has} other {# curriculum entries have}} no teacher, and the school's staffing policy refuses to generate a timetable until every entry has one. Staff the entries named here, or allow generation without a teacher in the staffing settings.
engineMessages.STAFF_NO_QUALIFIED_TEACHER_FOR_REQUIREME: {count, plural, one {# curriculum entry} other {# curriculum entries}} in {subject}{grades, select, any {} other { for years {grades}}} cannot be staffed: no active teacher holds a qualification that covers {count, plural, one {it} other {them}}. Record a qualification, or propose without respecting qualifications.
engineMessages.STAFF_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED_FOR_SUBJECT: {subject} needs {demandedMinutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} a week across {count, plural, one {# curriculum entry} other {# curriculum entries}}, and the teachers who may take them have at most {availableMinutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} left below their limits, so at least {shortMinutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} will stay unstaffed. Raise a target or the tolerance, record more qualifications, or reduce the subject's time.
engineMessages.STAFF_TEACHER_CAPACITY_ZERO: Already carries {fixedMinutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} a week against a limit of {limitMinutes}, so no further curriculum entry fits.
engineMessages.STAFF_MODEL_TOO_LARGE: There are too many possible teacher assignments to weigh in one go: about {variables} model variables against a limit of {limit}. Keep the entries that are settled as they are, or record qualifications so that fewer teachers are candidates for each entry, and try again.
engineMessages.TEACHER_LUNCH_WINDOW_TOO_NARROW: The teacher working-time rule {rule} guarantees a {minutes}-minute lunch inside {windowStart}-{windowEnd}, and that window holds {remaining, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} of the school day. Widen the window, shorten the lunch, or move it inside the hours the school teaches in.
engineMessages.TEACHER_LUNCH_LEAVES_NO_START: {causes, select, locked {Locked lessons} closed {Reservations on the teacher} locked_closed {Locked lessons and reservations on the teacher} other {These rules}} leave the teacher working-time rule {rule} no {minutes}-minute lunch inside {windowStart}-{windowEnd} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}}. Move a locked lesson, shorten the reservation, or widen the window.
engineMessages.TEACHER_REST_LONGER_THAN_THE_NIGHT: The teacher working-time rule {rule} asks for {restMinutes} minutes between the last lesson of one day and the first of the next, and the longest night this week can give is {nightMinutes} minutes: the teacher's {lessons, plural, one {# lesson} other {# lessons}} cannot all be placed on days that are not next to each other. Shorten the rest, lengthen the school day, or give this teacher fewer lessons.
engineMessages.TEACHER_LUNCH_HAS_NOWHERE_TO_GO: The {minutes}-minute lunch the teacher working-time rule {rule} guarantees inside {windowStart}-{windowEnd} on {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}} is one of the rules that cannot all hold at once: the teacher's lessons, the locked lessons and the reservations leave nowhere to put it. Widen the window, shorten the lunch, or free the middle of that day.
engineMessages.TEACHER_REST_CANNOT_BE_KEPT: The rest of {restMinutes} minutes that the teacher working-time rule {rule} asks for after {day, select, 1 {Monday} 2 {Tuesday} 3 {Wednesday} 4 {Thursday} 5 {Friday} 6 {Saturday} 7 {Sunday} other {day {day}}} is one of the rules that cannot all hold at once. Shorten the rest, or free the end of that day or the start of the next one.
